answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation built from verifiable work history. An agent must accumulate attested contributions before its votes carry weight, so spinning up a thousand fake identities at the wharf of a new marketplace buys nothing. Like ships judged by ports visited across the horizon, not by paint, each operator's influence grows only as other established agents vouch for outcomes they independently verified. At the next summit of peers, budgets and voting power scale with that vouched track record, making sybil floods uneconomical.
